alignments.note: Rule 55: a coordinator and a subordinator written together at the left edge of the waw's own recast clause are one rendering of that one connective morpheme; headed on the coordinator *And*, since the written morpheme is a coordinator. The competing head *when* is named here under rule 8.

Rule 17 gives the finite verb its subject pronoun, auxiliary and lexical verb, headed on *set*. Rule 33's closing paragraph gives it the *on* as well: *set ... on fire* is the only way English writes this predicate, so the word answers to the predicate's valency rather than stating what a bare nominal contributes. Discontinuous around *the brands* under rule 25.
Rule 12: the article assimilated into the pointed preposition is a real token and takes the written *the*.
`לַפִּיד` → *brands*, the ASV promoting the preposition's object to the direct object of *set*.

Rule 40: a `בְּ` whose object the ASV promotes to a direct object keeps nothing, exactly as the `בְּ` of *blew the trumpet* does. The competing reading gives this preposition the written *on*, but that word relates the setting to `אֵשׁ` rather than to the torches, and the subtraction test finds the torches' own relation unstated whether it stands or falls.
The written object noun `אֵשׁ` keeps its own *fire*; the preposition the English predicate needs to reach it is the predicate's under rule 33 and not this noun's.

Rule 17 gives the verb its subject pronoun and rule 44 heads a light verb plus complement on the word carrying the lexeme: *let* alone lets anything, so the head is *go*. The unit is discontinuous around the supplied object under rule 25.

Rule 44: no object morpheme stands in the clause — `יְשַׁלַּח` carries no suffix — so the supplied object pronoun answers to nothing and does not join the verb merely because it stands inside its rendering.
Rule 14: the ASV opens the apodosis bare, writing no connective for this waw, having already subordinated the preceding clause with *And when*.
Rule 11: the preposition takes the *into* written for it.

Rule 29: no article morpheme stands in the chain and the ASV writes a determiner before each noun's own word, so the construct takes the supplied *the*. Rule 31 heads on *standing*, since *grain* alone is any grain; the competing head *grain* was available.
Rule 19: the relational *of* belongs to the nomen rectum, with the supplied *the* standing before its own word under rule 29.
Rule 14: the waw takes the *and* written for it.
Rule 44: *up* is a phrasal particle completing the hiphil's consuming sense rather than a surplus the bare *burnt* has already written, so it stays with the verb and the head remains on the verb.
Rules 14 and 26: in a `מִן … עַד` range rendered *both … and*, the opening `מִן` is itself what the *both* says and takes it.
Rule 15: no article morpheme stands on the noun, so the supplied *the* joins the nominal expression; headed on the noun.
Rule 26: the waw standing where the connective stands takes the written *and*.
Rule 26: a `עַד` whose connective the waw beside it has already answered for is left unrendered.
Rule 15 gives the supplied *the* to the nominal expression; rule 31 heads on *standing* as in the first occurrence, the competing head *grain* being available.
Rule 14: the waw takes the *and* written for it.

Rule 51: the waw of this colon already holds the *and* written for it and is not a home for a second connective word, and no other morpheme in the clause licenses *also*; it is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them.
Rule 26: the waw beside it carries the phrase's connective, so this `עַד` is left with no English of its own.

Rule 30: one English word, *oliveyards*, writes both lexemes of the construct chain `כֶּרֶם זָיִת`, so the two morphemes share a unit; rule 23 heads it on the governing construct, since neither noun carries content the other lacks. The supplied *the* joins the expression under rule 15, no article morpheme standing in the phrase.

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment gave the *on* of *set the brands on fire* to the `בְּ` of `בַּלַּפִּידִים` (s004). That preposition governs the torches, which the ASV promotes to the bare direct object *the brands*, so rule 40's *blew the trumpet* case applies and the preposition is unrepresented; the *on* is the preposition the English predicate needs to reach `אֵשׁ`, and rule 33's closing paragraph assigns such a word to the predicate, since *set ... on fire* admits no other relation. The verb's unit is now t003, t004, t005, t008, headed on *set*, and `אֵשׁ` keeps the bare *fire*.
Token partition verified after correction: all 22 source ids and all 34 target ids are covered exactly once across 23 units.
The waw of the apodosis (s007) is unrepresented because the ASV spends its subordinating *when* on the first waw's own clause and opens the main clause bare.
Both `קָמָה` units are headed on *standing* under rule 31; *grain* is the defensible alternative and is named in each note.
*them* (t012) and *also* (t032) are the two supplied runs: no object morpheme stands with `יְשַׁלַּח`, and the waw of the last colon already holds its own *and*.
